issues.description: The Bitmap24 class member 'data' is declared with different types between header and implementation in the template repository (header declares 'int *data' while Bitmap24.cpp uses 'new char[...]' and treats 'data' as a char buffer). The solution repository consistently uses 'char *data'. This mismatch in the template will cause compilation/type errors and confuses students about the intended data type for pixel storage.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the Bitmap24::data member type consistent in the template. Change the declaration in example_program/src/Bitmap24.hpp from 'int *data;' to 'char *data;' so it matches the implementation (which allocates and treats the buffer as char[]) and the solution repository.

issues.description: The class member 'data' in example_program/src/Bitmap24.hpp is declared as an int* in the TEMPLATE_REPOSITORY but is used as a char* in Bitmap24.cpp (allocation, indexing, and fwrite). The SOLUTION_REPOSITORY header declares 'data' correctly as char*. This divergence means the same conceptual entity ('bitmap pixel buffer') is represented with different types/names across artifacts, causing compilation failures and unnecessary cognitive burden for students mapping the header to the implementation.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the member declaration in the template header match the implementation and solution: change 'int *data;' to 'char *data;' in example_program/src/Bitmap24.hpp (TEMPLATE_REPOSITORY). This aligns the conceptual 'bitmap buffer' type across header and implementation and matches the SOLUTION_REPOSITORY.
